en: A strong castle is our God,
a good defence and weapons.
He helps us free from every need
that has now befallen us.
The old evil foe
now means it in earnest.
Great might and much cunning
are his cruel armour.
On earth there is none his equal.
With our own might nothing is done;
we are very soon lost.
There fights for us the right man,
whom God himself has chosen.
Do you ask who that is?
He is called Jesus Christ,
the Lord Sabaoth,
and there is no other God.
He must hold the field.
And if the world were full of devils
and wanted to swallow us up entirely,
we are not so very afraid;
we shall still prevail.
The prince of this world,
however grim he makes himself look,
can still do nothing to us.
That is because he is judged.
One little word can fell him.
The Word they shall let stand
and have no thanks for it.
He is with us, indeed, on the field
with his Spirit and gifts.
If they take the body,
goods, honour, child and wife,
let them go.
They gain nothing by it.
The kingdom must still remain ours.
notes: line 1.1: 'Burg' is a castle or stronghold.
line 2.7: 'Zebaoth' (Sabaoth) is the Hebrew title 'of hosts', i.e. the Lord of the heavenly armies; kept as a name.
line 3.8: 'er ist gericht't' = he has been judged (condemned), after John 16:11.
line 4.2: 'kein' Dank dazu haben' is read as 'and get no thanks for it' (they must leave the Word alone, like it or not); the phrase is often glossed 'whether they like it or not'.
line 4.3: 'auf dem Plan' = on the battlefield.
line 4.7: 'Laß fahren dahin' = let it go, let it all be gone.
